title: The little way
hookLine: Thérèse of Lisieux: small things done with great love

lines: A YOUNG NUN WANTS TO BE A SAINT.
A GRAIN OF SAND BESIDE A MOUNTAIN.
cards: In a Carmelite convent in Lisieux, in France, a young nun named Thérèse wanted to be a saint. But when she measured herself against the great saints, she writes, she felt like a grain of sand beside a mountain.

She would never do anything that size. She was going to spend her life in a small enclosed house, doing laundry and chores, praying with the same few women every day. So she went looking for another road.

teach.b: Thérèse tells this in her memoir, Story of a Soul, and her pictures are homely. First, the elevator. She'd heard of elevators, an invention, she notes, that lifted people so they didn't have to climb.
Too small, she writes, to climb the rough staircase of perfection, she wanted an elevator, and decided it was the arms of Jesus, lifting the little ones who can't climb.
Second, flowers. Love, she says, proves itself by deeds, and she had no great deeds to give. So she would strew flowers: every small sacrifice, every glance, every kind word, offered with love.
Nothing was too small to count. Third, the hardest one.

There was a sister in the convent whose manner, Thérèse admits, she found deeply disagreeable. So she set out to treat that sister as she would the person she loved most, smiling whenever they met and praying for her.
One day, she writes, the sister asked what it was about her that Thérèse found so attractive.
Fourth, the center: a discovery she writes about, that in the heart of the Church, her vocation would be love. Not a role. A way of doing every small thing.

Catholics honor her as a saint. Some readers find her way fits small lives: a nurse on night shift, a parent of toddlers, anyone whose day is mostly ordinary. In her way of seeing, the size of the act isn't the measure.

how: Catholics who follow Thérèse's little way offer small daily tasks and kindnesses to God, and some ask her prayers as Saint Thérèse, the Little Flower.

s: Thérèse planned great missions to become a saint
she felt like a grain of sand beside a mountain, and looked for a little way instead.

games.q: you're Thérèse. a sister in your small convent rubs you the wrong way every single day. what do you do?
o: keep your distance as politely as you can.
treat her as you would the one you love most.
ask to be moved to another task.
games.why: she smiled at her and prayed for her, until the sister asked what it was about her Thérèse found so attractive.

practice: Run through the next few hours in your mind and pick the most ordinary thing waiting there: a dish, an email, a diaper, a commute, a line at the store.
Picture doing that exact thing with great care, for someone, the way Thérèse strewed flowers: not faster, not bigger, just with love inside it.
Notice how small it is and let that be fine, and if you pray, you can offer it, the way she did.

wordCard.voice: Lisieux, the French convent where Thérèse, feeling like a grain of sand beside a mountain, found her own little way to love in small deeds. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: a grain of sand. Small, and still counted. Tomorrow, a name for God.
